 PREACHING HATE 
 Hasan Piker compares suburban Jewish voters to white supremacists in online rant
 Abdul El-Sayed called the comments ‘utterly inappropriate and flat out wrong’ — without criticizing Piker himself
 Posters of influencer Hasan Piker on easels before a New York City mayoral campaign press conference (Photo by Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
 By 
 Marc Rod 
 October 30, 2026 
 SHARE Share options Facebook 
 Telegram 
 LinkedIn 
 WhatsApp 
 Reddit 
 Add JewishInsider on Google 
 In a screaming rant on his livestream on Friday, antisemitic influencer Hasan Piker compared the heavily Jewish community of West Bloomfield in the Detroit suburbs to a Ku Klux Klan neighborhood, describing it as full of Jewish supremacists. Piker’s monologue led Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed to condemn Piker’s comments as “inappropriate” without speaking out against Piker himself.
Piker, while watching a news segment about West Bloomfield and a group of canvassers for El-Sayed in the district, said, “I don’t think this is insensitive to say — this is the equivalent of going to that like KKK neighborhood to stump for a Black candidate who’s running expressly … to abolish anti-miscegenation laws.”
 He said that, while the Jewish community in West Bloomfield might be aesthetically different, “the supremacist attitude underlying their worldview is identical. … It’s racial supremacy. It’s Jewish supremacy.”
 “Thank god they probably don’t own any guns,” he added.
 Responding to a person interviewed in the news segment who said that maintaining Israel as a safe haven for Jews is important to the Jewish community, Piker began shouting.
 “Look at how beautiful your neighborhood is. What are you talking about, having a safe haven? You would never live in Israel … Even the thought of it disgusts you,” he continued. “If it’s so dangerous, go live in Israel. Oh you won’t?”
 He continued, “You f***ing idiot, you f***ing moron, you’re making this place that you live less safe and worse overall by voting for a f***ing Republican. … ‘I’m voting at the behest of Israel for Mike Rogers, who is the Christian version of Itamar Ben-Gvir.’ What is wrong with you? You f***ing psycho. What the f*** are you talking about? You’d never live in Israel, but now you’re f***ing up America. America is going to resemble all the worst qualities of Israel that you don’t like.”
 Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, who campaigned repeatedly with Piker during the primary, condemned Piker’s comments in a statement to Jewish Insider , though he didn’t mention Piker by name. 
 “I grew up in the town over from West Bloomfield. Comparing Jewish Michiganders to the Ku Klux Klan is utterly inappropriate and flat out wrong,” El-Sayed said. “From day one, my campaign has been focused on rallying Michiganders of all stripes together into a movement that will bridge divides, not separate us more. Our canvassers will continue to knock doors and have important conversations with voters in every corner of the state.” 
 State Rep. Noah Arbit, who represents the community in the state legislature, told Jewish Insider that Piker’s words may incite violence against his community. Arbit told JI that he found the clip, “disgusting, repugnant,” “insane,” “irresponsible” and an “incitement to violence.”
 “This is exactly the kind of rhetoric that will breed violence,” he said. “Talking about West Bloomfield’s Jewish community as if it is the KKK, some white supremacist community, is exactly the kind of vile, dangerous, radicalizing rhetoric that will no doubt encourage people who have already been radicalized to come and take up violence against us.”
 West Bloomfield is home to Temple Israel, the site of a Hezbollah-inspired terrorist attack earlier this year. Arbit said that local police will need to be notified about the clip and that the community will have to take extra precautions after having been singled out in such a way.
 Arbit also emphasized that the clip is likely to hurt El-Sayed in the closing days of the campaign, “to attack the character of a community that is going to be a pivotal community in the election on Tuesday.” Arbit has said he plans to leave his ballot blank for the Senate race.
 “This is exactly why we have asked Abdul El-Sayed time and time again to disavow Hasan Piker. I don’t believe that Abdul believes those things about West Bloomfield Township, but this was one of his biggest campaign surrogates,” Arbit told JI, before El-Sayed released his statement. “It is his responsibility to disavow these attacks on people that Abdul hoped will be his constituents.”
 After El-Sayed condemned the comments, Arbit offered his thanks.
“As I said, I never believed any of our Democratic candidates share these heinous views about West Bloomfield, and am grateful to [El-Sayed] for joining me in firmly rejecting Hasan Piker’s hate and bigotry against my community,” he wrote on X.
 Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) said that Piker’s “rant … should be condemned loudly.”
 “It is anti-semitic, divisive and deeply offensive,” she said.  “I get that this is what he does for attention. But flippantly attacking a proud, diverse community — not to mention a political organizer doing the most American of things in our democratic process — reveals how misguided and uninformed he actually is about Michigan.”
Arbit told JI that any candidate, regardless of party affiliation, running in the state “should have no problem unequivocally denouncing these putrid, vile comments about my community.”
“Every person, especially those who have counted on this person as an ally, as someone that they have campaigned with, needs to denounce these comments immediately,” Arbit continued. “Because it puts my community — not just the Jewish community of West Bloomfield but every person in West Bloomfield — in danger.”
 He added in a Facebook post that the sentiments expressed by Piker are antithetical to what his community stands for.
 “West Bloomfield is a bulwark against his hate, and we will never, ever allow hate — his or anyone else’s — to overwhelm us or distract us from continuing to build the wonderful, strong community that we are,” he said.
 State Sen. Jeremy Moss, who is running to represent the Congressional district that includes West Bloomfield, emphasized the trauma that the community has already faced.
 “West Bloomfield is a beautiful, welcoming, and diverse community that has been through a lot this year already. After spending a whole campaign putting a target on Oakland County’s Jewish community, Hasan Piker is the last person who should be antagonizing these voters,” Moss said on X. “He is a plague here and these feelings of anguish are the result. He should keep West Bloomfield out of his mouth.”
